rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3-2.4 and 3 - the authors run their own GIS-based multi-criteria evaluation (AHP weighted overlay) of seven factors for Uganda, compute rainfall deficits from 1990-2020 station data, produce baseline and two future-scenario suitability maps, and ground-truth the baseline map against five existing irrigation schemes.
rows.notes: The study is a GIS/AHP land-suitability mapping exercise for surface irrigation in Uganda under climate-change scenarios. It does not involve artificial intelligence, machine learning from historical data, app-based or decision-support scheduling, or any measurement of irrigation efficiency or water conservation. Its results are areal percentages of land in suitability classes (e.g., 0.9% highly suitable, 32.4% moderately suitable) and how these shift under warming scenarios. It offers no evidence on the claimed technology (AI/app scheduling) or effect (water conservation / improved irrigation performance).

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is unrelated to the cited claim about AI-driven irrigation decision-making; it is a GIS multi-criteria land-suitability assessment for surface irrigation.
